title: Isaiah Chapter 65 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 65 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 65 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 65.

questions.question: Who is sought by those who did not ask for Him?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'I am sought of them that asked not for me;' referring to the LORD in Isaiah 65:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the people He has spread His hands to?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that He has spread out His hands unto a 'rebellious people' in Isaiah 65:2.

questions.question: What actions provoke the LORD to anger according to Isaiah 65?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the people 'sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick,' provoking the LORD's anger in Isaiah 65:3.

questions.question: True or False: The people mentioned in Isaiah 65:4 eat swine's flesh.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:4 explicitly states that the people 'which eat swine's flesh.'

questions.question: What do the people say in Isaiah 65:5?
questions.explanation: The verse contains the statement 'Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me;' indicating their attitude in Isaiah 65:5.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will keep silence according to Isaiah 65:6.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I will not keep silence,' indicating that the LORD will speak rather than remain silent in Isaiah 65:6.

questions.question: What will the LORD recompense into their bosom according to Isaiah 65:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:6 mentions the recompense will be 'even recompense into their bosom' for their iniquities.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will create in Isaiah 65:17?
options: New heavens and a new earth
questions.correctAnswer: New heavens and a new earth
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states 'For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth' in Isaiah 65:17.

questions.question: True or False: The former troubles will be remembered in the new creation.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 mentions that 'the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.'

questions.question: What will happen to the wolf and the lamb according to Isaiah 65:25?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'The wolf and the lamb shall feed together,' indicating peace among creatures in Isaiah 65:25.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise His servants will do in Isaiah 65:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:13 promises that 'my servants shall eat,' contrasting with the fate of others.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65, what comes first in the actions of the people?
questions.explanation: The first action mentioned is 'But ye are they that forsake the LORD' in Isaiah 65:11.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 65 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 65 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 65:10, what will Sharon become for the people that have sought the Lord?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:10 states that Sharon shall be a fold of flocks for my people that have sought me, indicating a place of peace and provision for those who seek God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:13 say will happen to those who forsake the Lord?
options: They will eat and drink abundantly
They shall be hungry and thirsty
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be hungry and thirsty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:13 declares that those who forsake the Lord will be hungry and thirsty, contrasting their fate with that of God's servants who will be provided for.

questions.question: What is the fate described for the people who did not answer when God called, according to Isaiah 65:12?
options: They will be numbered to the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will be numbered to the sword
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:12 states that those who did not respond to God's call and chose evil will be numbered to the sword, indicating judgment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 65:15, what will happen to the name of those who forsake the Lord?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:15 indicates that those who forsake the Lord will leave their name for a curse, highlighting the consequences of turning away from God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 65:18, God creates Jerusalem as a place of mourning and despair.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:18 states that God creates Jerusalem as a rejoicing and her people as a joy, which directly contradicts the statement.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:14 promise will happen to God's servants?
options: They will sing for joy of heart
questions.correctAnswer: They will sing for joy of heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:14 promises that God's servants shall sing for joy of heart, indicating the blessings that come from faithfulness to God.

questions.question: What is indicated in Isaiah 65:16 about those who bless themselves?
options: They should bless themselves in the God of truth
They will forget the former troubles
They will prosper in all things
questions.correctAnswer: They should bless themselves in the God of truth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:16 indicates that those who bless themselves should do so in the God of truth, emphasizing reliance on God for true blessings.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 65:24 states that God will answer before they call.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:24 states that before they call, God will answer, illustrating God's readiness to respond to the needs of His people.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 65:17, what does God promise to create?
options: New heavens and a new earth
questions.correctAnswer: New heavens and a new earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 promises that God will create new heavens and a new earth, signifying a transformative future for His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 65:11 connect to the consequences mentioned in Isaiah 65:12?
options: Forsaking the Lord leads to blessings
Forsaking the Lord leads to being numbered to the sword
Remembering the holy mountain leads to prosperity
Preparing a table for the troop leads to joy
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking the Lord leads to being numbered to the sword
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:11 describes forsaking the Lord, which directly leads to the consequences of judgment described in Isaiah 65:12.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:19 say will no longer be heard in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:19 states that the voice of weeping will be no more heard in Jerusalem, indicating a time of joy and restoration.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 65:23 assures that God's people will labor in vain.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:23 states that God's people shall not labor in vain, assuring that their efforts will be fruitful and rewarding.

questions.question: What do verses 20-23 collectively signify about the nature of life in the new creation God promises?
options: Life will be filled with suffering
Life will be short and unfulfilled
Life will be characterized by longevity and enjoyment of labor
Life will be chaotic and disordered
questions.correctAnswer: Life will be characterized by longevity and enjoyment of labor
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 emphasize that in the new creation, people will live long lives and enjoy the fruits of their labor, contrasting with former hardships.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 65 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 65.

questions.question: What will no longer be heard in Jerusalem according to Isaiah 65:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:19 states that the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, indicating a time of joy and peace in Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:20, what age is mentioned for a child who shall die?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:20 mentions that the child shall die an hundred years old, emphasizing a long life expectancy in the new creation.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 65:22, who will enjoy the work of their hands?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:22 states that mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands, indicating a blessing on God's chosen people.

questions.question: Which animal is mentioned as eating straw like a bullock in Isaiah 65:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:25 describes the lion eating straw like the bullock, signifying peace among creatures in the new creation.

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 65:24, it states that God will answer before His people call.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:24 confirms that before they call, I will answer, highlighting God's readiness to respond to His people's needs.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:18 say God will create in the future?
options: New heavens and a new earth
questions.correctAnswer: New heavens and a new earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 declares that God will create new heavens and a new earth, indicating a complete renewal of creation.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:12, what is the consequence for those who did not answer God's call?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:12 indicates that those who did not answer God's call will be numbered to the sword, demonstrating divine judgment.

questions.question: Which theme from Isaiah 65:19 is echoed in Revelation 21:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:19's promise of no more weeping is echoed in Revelation 21:4, where God wipes away every tear and there is no more pain.

questions.question: What will happen in the Valley of Achor according to Isaiah 65:10?
options: It will be a place for herds to lie down
It will be filled with idols
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place for herds to lie down
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:10 describes the Valley of Achor as a place for herds to lie down, signifying peace and abundance for God's people.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 65:15, the name of the wicked will be left as a blessing.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:15 states that the wicked shall leave their name for a curse, indicating their condemnation rather than blessing.

questions.question: What does the term 'blessed' in Isaiah 65:23 signify in Hebrew?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'blessed' signifies happiness or being favored by God, which aligns with the promise in Isaiah 65:23.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:6, what does God say He will do regarding the rebellious people's iniquities?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:6 states that God will not keep silence but will recompense their iniquities into their bosom, indicating judgment.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Isaiah 65:22 when discussing the days of a tree?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:22 uses simile when comparing the days of God's people to the days of a tree, suggesting longevity and stability.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Isaiah 65:8 and Matthew 9:17 regarding new wine?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:8 speaks of new wine found in the cluster, indicating renewal, which parallels Matthew 9:17's teaching about new wine needing new bottles.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 65 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 65 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:1 reveal about God's outreach to those who do not seek Him?
options: He only seeks those who ask for Him
He is sought by those that do not ask for Him
He ignores those who do not seek Him
He is found only by a chosen few
questions.correctAnswer: He is sought by those that do not ask for Him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:1 states that God is sought by those who did not ask for Him, demonstrating His grace and initiative in salvation, consistent with Romans 3:11.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:2, what does God mean by spreading out His hands to a rebellious people?
options: He is welcoming them with love
He is preparing to punish them
He is indifferent to their actions
He is calling them to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: He is calling them to repentance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:2 indicates God's desire for His people to turn back to Him, emphasizing His patience and readiness to receive them despite their rebellion, similar to Matthew 23:37.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face' in Isaiah 65:3 indicate about the nature of sin?
options: Sin is a personal affront to God
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is a personal affront to God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:3 describes the persistent rebellion of the people as a direct provocation to God, highlighting the seriousness of their sin as a personal offense to Him, as seen in Numbers 14:18.

questions.question: Isaiah 65:4 mentions eating swine's flesh as an abominable act. What does this signify in terms of the law provided to Israel?
options: It shows God's acceptance of all foods
It highlights the importance of ceremonial purity
It indicates a lack of divine standards
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the importance of ceremonial purity
questions.explanation: The reference to swine's flesh in Isaiah 65:4 underscores the ceremonial laws given to Israel, which included dietary restrictions meant to signify holiness, as seen in Leviticus 11:7.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:8 convey about God's attitude toward His faithful servants?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:8 illustrates God's intention to preserve and bless His faithful servants, using the metaphor of new wine in a cluster to signify their value, akin to Matthew 25:21.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:12, what consequence does God state for those who do not respond to His call?
options: They will be numbered to the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will be numbered to the sword
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:12 clearly states that those who did not respond to God's call would face dire consequences, symbolizing judgment, reflecting the seriousness of rejecting divine invitation as seen in Matthew 22:14.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:13 contrast between God's servants and the rebellious people?
options: God's servants will be rich, the others poor
God's servants will eat, the others will be hungry
God's servants will labor, the others will rest
God's servants will travel, the others will stay
questions.correctAnswer: God's servants will eat, the others will be hungry
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:13 presents a stark contrast showing that while God's servants will be provided for, the rebellious will suffer hunger, emphasizing God's provision for the righteous, similar to Psalm 37:25.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:17, what promise does God give about the future creation?
options: He will create new heavens and a new earth
He will restore the old earth
He will leave creation as it is
questions.correctAnswer: He will create new heavens and a new earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 declares God's creative power to bring about a new order, symbolizing hope and renewal, which is echoed in Revelation 21:1.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:19 reveal about God's relationship with Jerusalem and His people?
options: He will rejoice and bring joy to His people
questions.correctAnswer: He will rejoice and bring joy to His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:19 expresses God's deep joy in His people and their city, indicating His loving commitment to restore and bless, as seen in Zephaniah 3:17.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 65:22, what assurance is given regarding labor in the new creation?
options: They will not enjoy the fruits of their labor
They will not labor in vain
questions.correctAnswer: They will not labor in vain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:22 assures that God's people will enjoy the fruits of their labor, emphasizing the meaningfulness and satisfaction of work in His restored creation, which aligns with Colossians 3:23.

questions.question: In Isaiah 65:24, what does God promise regarding communication with His people?
options: He will not listen to them
He will answer before they call
He will only listen to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: He will answer before they call
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:24 indicates God's readiness to respond to His people, illustrating His intimate relationship with them and His proactive care, reflecting 1 John 5:14.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 65:25 illustrate about the nature of peace in the new creation?
options: There will be harmony in creation
questions.correctAnswer: There will be harmony in creation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:25 portrays a future where even predators and prey coexist peacefully, symbolizing complete restoration and harmony in God's creation, akin to Romans 8:21.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God does not care about the choices of people and their outcomes. What does Isaiah 65:12-13 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to human choices
God actively responds to the choices of people
God only blesses the chosen people
God does not punish wrong choices
questions.correctAnswer: God actively responds to the choices of people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:12-13 illustrates that God holds people accountable for their choices and actively responds to them, indicating His engagement and concern for the consequences of their actions, similar to Ezekiel 18:30.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 65:6 and verse 7 convey about divine justice?
options: God is unjust in His dealings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:6-7 reveals that God will not remain silent regarding sin and will hold people accountable for their iniquities, affirming His justice and righteousness, which is consistent with Galatians 6:7.

questions.question: How do Isaiah 65:15 and 19 collectively express God's attitude towards His chosen people?
options: He will bring them joy and restore their name
He will punish them without hope
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring them joy and restore their name
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:15 and 19 together illustrate that while there is judgment for the unfaithful, God ultimately desires to restore joy and a new identity for His chosen people, aligning with Jeremiah 29:11.
